			56 container challenge
				57 heading Overview, Value: 2
					58 text Overview
				59 text This skill teaches the agent to turn a messy bundle of data, findings, and requests into a tightly reasoned executive presentation storyline.
				60 text Given a strategic input (a prose brief, a data table, a bullet findings list, or an existing deck outline) together with an audience and a decision, a good result is a complete, structured output: a single governing thought that the evidence actually supports, a MECE argument tree with two to four branches, an action-title slide list where every headline is a complete so-what sentence, per-slide content specifications, and a self-check flag report.
				61 text The submission is a SKILL.md, with optional reference files the agent opens by name when SKILL.md directs it. Strong skills teach the agent a reasoning procedure it can apply to inputs it has never seen before: how to read footnotes before forming a claim, how to test headline flow, how to match a chart type to a claim rather than to data shape. Weak skills paste in template outlines or memorised slide structures that collapse the moment surface details change.
				62 text A skill built to memorise specific scenarios will not hold up as challenges evolve.
				63 text You submit a skill: a SKILL.md and, if you need them, reference files it points at. A fixed base agent loads it and answers all 7 scenarios with it, then returns a scored breakdown. The submission that holds the top of the leaderboard accrues on-chain emissions for as long as it stays first.
				64 text We are looking for skills that demonstrate good design and help the agent perform like a capable practitioner in this domain.
			65 container requirements
				66 heading Requirements (7 Tests), Value: 2
					67 text Requirements (7 Tests)
				68 text Your skill is tested across 5 capability types, with 7 scenarios in total. Every submission is evaluated against all 7 scenarios. There is no sampling, so consistent quality across every capability type counts.
				69 table
					70 row
						71 cell

					77 row
						78 cell
							79 text Type A: Contradiction handling
						80 cell
							81 text This type tests whether the agent correctly identifies that the input evidence refutes the requested conclusion rather than silently building the requested storyline. The skill must teach the agent to surface the contradiction first, offer two governing thought options (one evidence-supported, one requester-preferred), and then storyline only the evidence-supported one unless the requester explicitly redirects.
						82 cell
							83 text 1
					84 row
						85 cell
							86 text Type B: Existing deck repair
						87 cell
							88 text This type tests whether the agent can diagnose and improve a deck that already exists rather than rebuild from scratch. The skill must teach the agent to extract the implicit governing thought from the current outline, run a headline-flow test across the existing slide titles, and prefer reordering and retitling over wholesale reconstruction.
						89 cell
							90 text 1
					91 row
						92 cell
							93 text Type C: Missing decision clarification
						94 cell
							95 text This type tests whether the agent stops appropriately when the input contains no actionable decision or named audience, rather than inventing one and proceeding. The skill must teach the agent to issue a focused clarifying question and to offer two or more plausible decisions the data could plausibly serve, so the requester has concrete options to react to.
						96 cell
							97 text 1
					98 row
						99 cell
							100 text Type D: Standard storyline with counter-evidence
						101 cell
							102 text This type tests whether the agent builds a complete MECE argument tree that includes material counter-evidence rather than omitting inconvenient findings. The skill must teach the agent to construct two to four branches where each branch is a one-sentence claim citing specific input evidence, and to place counter-evidence inside the tree rather than suppressing it.
						103 cell
							104 text 1
					105 row
						106 cell
							107 text Type E: Standard storyline with footnote effects
						108 cell
							109 text This type tests whether the agent reads footnotes, unit labels, and period qualifiers before forming the governing thought, rather than skimming the headline numbers. The skill must teach the agent to compute relevant deltas, check whether notes materially change what the data shows, and produce a governing thought that reflects the footnote-adjusted picture rather than the surface reading.
						110 cell

				121 text Sealed reference set
				122 text The scenarios with their reference outputs and grading notes. Validators grade against it; it is published when the challenge closes. Committed hash, sha256:
				123 text 0d14d68d0b928a0b1b87bb0a861490fd4954709af07393b69e23016ca14066b3
				124 text When you submit, we run your skill through a standardised base agent provided by sundae_bar. The base agent is the same for every submission and is not supplied by you. It receives the challenge's test scenarios one at a time, calls the load_skill tool to read your SKILL.md and the list of your reference files, opens a reference with read_reference when your SKILL.md tells it to, and follows the skill to answer each scenario.
				125 text Same base agent, same tests, only the submitted skill changes. Scores therefore reflect the quality of your skill, not agent configuration: the agent's answers are only as good as the procedure your skill teaches.
				126 text Graders then score each answer for output quality, correct skill use, and gaming behavior, and the per-scenario scores are averaged into your challenge score.
				127 container
					128 text What is public at open:  the scenario inputs, the rubric, and the sha256 hash of the sealed reference set (the same scenarios with their reference outputs and grading notes). Validators grade against the sealed set; the hash on the challenge page is your proof that it cannot change while the challenge runs.
				129 container
					130 text What you see while it runs:  your total, a score for every scenario and every grader, and the written notes of the gate checks (dataset derivation, skill alignment, redundancy, novelty). The quality judges' written explanations are held back, because they describe the reference answer.
				131 container
					132 text What is published when the challenge closes:  the sealed reference set, every judge explanation, and the full validator outputs for every submission. Check the file against the published hash and re-run any evaluation yourself.
				133 container
					134 text What you submit:  a folder or a .zip with SKILL.md at the top level and an optional references/ folder. A single SKILL.md is also accepted. All files are the submission.
				135 container
					136 text Limits:  SKILL.md is at most 10,000 bytes and is always loaded. references/ holds up to 30 files, each at most 32,000 characters, 128,000 characters in total. Text formats only: .md, .txt, .json, .yaml, .yml and .csv. Lower-case file names using letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores. The current values are published by the platform API at GET /api/v2/submissions/limits; the submission form reads them from there.
				137 container
					138 text How references are read:  the agent always sees SKILL.md plus a list of your reference file names. It opens a reference only when SKILL.md tells it to, by name. Each read is one harness step within a cap of 10 steps per scenario, and the file's text counts against the scenario's token budget of 30,000 tokens. A reference the agent never opens does nothing for the score.
				139 container
					140 text Rejected at upload:  HTML comments, images, scripts, hidden or invisible characters, nested archives, disallowed file types, and anything over a limit. Text addressed to the evaluators, or that tries to override instructions, is accepted but places the entry under review and scores zero.
				141 container
					142 text Important:  the base-agent harness is fixed at evaluation time and its available tools are load_skill, read_reference. You submit only skill files; you cannot supply your own agent, add tools, or alter the base agent's configuration.
				143 container
					144 text Tip:  write your skill as though you are onboarding a capable new hire who needs a procedure, not scripting a chatbot.

				183 heading How to submit, Value: 3
					184 text How to submit
				185 text 1 Login or create a sundaebar.ai account
				186 text Create an account and add your Bittensor wallet ID to your profile to earn alpha rewards in the challenge.
				187 text 2 Review the requirements
				188 text Review the reference skills (good, mediocre, gaming) to understand the quality bar and calibration points.
				189 text 3 Build your skill
				190 text Draft your SKILL.md (at most 10,000 bytes; it is always loaded) and, if the method needs them, put tables, templates and worked examples in reference files under references/. Tell the agent in SKILL.md which reference to open and when, by file name. Focus on teaching procedure rather than providing templates.
				191 text 4 Test locally

					214 text Rewards
				215 text Emissions accrue on-chain to whichever submission currently holds the top of the leaderboard. There is no fixed per-submission payout: the current leader earns for as long as it stays first.
				216 text Time at the top takes all. A strong skill submitted early starts accruing immediately and keeps earning until another submission displaces it. Once you are displaced, accrual stops until you reclaim the top.
				217 text Rankings shift as others iterate. Get to the top early, then keep refining your skill to defend the position.
				218 text Every file in your submission is scanned at submission time by a skill integrity gate: your SKILL.md and every reference file, whether or not your skill points at it. The gate checks that your skill teaches procedure rather than encoding scenario-specific content from our evaluation pool. Content placed in a reference file is checked exactly as content in SKILL.md.
				219 text A skill that fails the integrity gate scores 0 for the submission. The gate runs deterministically and reports its finding as part of your results. This is how the evaluation framework stays credible: a high score should reflect a skill that genuinely teaches procedure, not one that memorised our test set.
